note: Every case in tests/host_launch_diagnostics.rs is an execution of instrumented production code through an existing public seam of the eliot_host library target (HostLaunchOptions::{parse,parse_system_service,validate_service_main_argv}, classify_host_scm_inspection, validate_host_scm_bootstrap driven to its pre-SCM refusal, publish_supervision_record_table driven to its publication refusal). The facade is never called directly from the test target, so no expected log record is hand-constructed and no case compares the facade to itself. Records are read back out of a scoped tracing subscriber after real production code ran. Boundaries whose owner is a private module behind pub(super) items (host_job_launch, launch_artifact_lease, launch_descriptor_validation, store_kernel_launch_sequence, kernel_activation_driver, kernel_front_door_client) are proven by inline #[cfg(test)] cases in their owning file; the integration case names the owner and asserts the private source binding (see inline_case_owners and unreachable_positive_arms). Audit 5910159678: the two false readiness phase tokens are retired (see renamed_phase_tokens) and the frozen structured correlation now carries the owner-held identities. Sink outcome never alters result/order/status/cleanup. Package fixtures never claim live launch. Real Windows Event Log delivery smoke needs #984 and stays an honest residual: the Event Log seam reports the platform's own live answer - available on Windows where #984's safe port is live, typed EventLogUnavailable off Windows - while the facade's own Event Log arm stays typed EventLogUnavailable on every platform because it routes to tracing only. No fixture drives a real OS report, no FFI is acquired in Host, and no delivery is faked either way. Audit 5910159678 follow-up (W2/AUD3): the correlated entry points that close the forwarded-correlation defect are recorded under correlated_entry_points, forwarded_correlation_contour, forwarded_refusal_arms and forwarded_reason_arms, and executed_forwarded_correlation names the one seam per case whose phase record this target can really execute against an already-held handle, so every claim about forwarded identities is read out of a captured record rather than asserted from prose.

key_meanings.operation: operation names one identity in the activation pair: the canonical KernelRecord operation identity, the labelled-UUID handle kernel_activation_driver.rs binds from current.operation.operation_id or permit.operation_id. NOT every transition is rendered: the driver mints seven operation ids (kernel-candidate-shadow, kernel-handoff-prepared, kernel-prior-disposition, kernel-nonce-issued, kernel-activating, kernel-active, kernel-activation-failed) but only some reach a record - the fail observed record deliberately renders the PRE-transition id, because the transition it is about has not committed yet. "Re-minted per transition" describes the minter (crate-level `operation` fn), not the set of rendered records. Every kernel_front_door_client.rs call site renders operation=missing: no closure that builds one of those correlations holds that identity, so naming it there would mean re-deriving it. Neither the wire message id (activation id plus a sequence suffix) nor the activation id itself may fill the key, and the wire identity is never parsed back into the activation id. RECORDED LOSS: the reconcile family binds no identity at all (its body is NONE plus an optional reason), so those records carry the phase token and the typed reason kind only - the wire message identity they previously named under operation is rendered nowhere, and the frozen eight-key vocabulary has no slot for a per-message wire identity. RECORDED LOSS, ALSO: scm_launch.rs binds no operation identity at all - not one call site in that file passes one - so every record it emits renders operation=missing, exactly like every other site that does not hold that identity. That file always held a real, non-secret, owner-held identity in hand, the Windows SCM service name (ServiceRegistrationRequest::service_name), and it is rendered nowhere under this key: the name survives in typed form only, in HostScmRegistrationCause::Absent and in InstalledCandidateReadback::service_name, both of which are unchanged. This is a loss of rendered detail, not a claim that the name is unavailable, unobservable, or unimportant.
key_meanings.fence: fence does NOT mean one identity across the corpus. It means the candidate activation id on all TEN front-door and kernel-activation sites, matching DurableKernelActivationDriver's record_fence(host, activation_id, activation_generation) binding, and it means TWO further identities inside host_job_launch.rs: the StateFence authority-epoch LINEAGE id at that file's bind and launch sites, and the Host installation epoch's LINEAGE id at its resume and start sites. Those are distinct types (StateFence::authority_epoch: EpochId versus HostInstallationEpoch::epoch: EpochTransition), so under I14.20 line 296 they are not interchangeable. This is a REAL RESIDUAL COLLISION, escalated and deliberately not resolved here: unifying them is a cross-file contract change. Binding the Kernel authority epoch lineage/sequence into fence in the two activation files was RETIRED by this delivery, so in those two files the epoch reaches no correlation slot - but host_job_launch.rs still renders a lineage under the same key, and that is the collision, not a settled difference. The epoch stays compared for real on the semantic path wherever it decides an owner proof.
key_meanings.process_start: process_start names ONE identity, the Host-observed Kernel Job root process START identity: the Job root pid together with the handle-observed creation time, rendered in the owner's own shape as pid:<root_pid>:start:<root_start_time_100ns>. It is the start pair, never the pid alone, because a pid is reusable and a process-start identity is not: PID alone, file existence, IPC acknowledgement or exit zero is not readiness or ownership, so no call site on any of the eight files may fill this key with a bare reusable pid. In kernel_activation_driver.rs the value is projected from the retained KernelRecord candidate_job_binding alone - read from binding.root_pid and binding.root_start_time_100ns, through the file's own kernel_process_start_identity projection - on EVERY call site whose record retains one: resume requested, bind requested, candidate observed, nonce requested, nonce issued, activating requested, activation observed, readiness observed and fail observed. Nothing is re-derived, re-read, re-verified or probed to obtain it, and it is never taken from a Kernel-authored process handle; where a record retained NO Job binding (the pre-bind shadow record the resume fixture builds) the slot renders the explicit process_start=missing marker instead, and that absence is a fact about the record, not a claim that a resume or any other step never holds the identity. A Kernel process id that arrives as opaque receipt or request text is NOT a process start identity and is not bound into this key. Only THREE of the other seven files own a start-pair projection and bind this key: host_launch_options.rs does not bind process_start at all (its admitted correlation binds only installation, generation and artifact), and neither do launch_artifact_lease.rs, launch_descriptor_validation.rs or store_kernel_launch_sequence.rs - the last of those emits six phase records and binds only `reason`. The three that do project their own owner start pair are host_job_launch.rs::host_launch_process_start_identity, scm_launch.rs::scm_process_start_identity and kernel_front_door_client.rs::front_door_process_start_identity; a call site holding no such pair renders the explicit missing marker. Two spellings exist for the same fact: windows-pid:<pid>:start:<t> in host_job_launch.rs and scm_launch.rs, and pid:<pid>:start:<t> in kernel_activation_driver.rs and kernel_front_door_client.rs. A reader correlating across files must translate, and unifying the spelling is a cross-file change that is escalated, not decided here.
key_meanings.generation: generation is NOT one identity across the corpus and this is a REAL RESIDUAL, escalated and not resolved here. Every value is a u64, so nothing at the type boundary separates them, and a reader cannot tell two records apart by eye. It carries FOUR quantities: the immutable transaction-plan generation (host_launch_options.rs, scm_launch.rs); the approved runtime ResourceGeneration (host_job_launch.rs, launch_descriptor_validation.rs, kernel_activation_driver.rs, kernel_front_door_client.rs); the activation-generation EPOCH SEQUENCE (kernel_activation_driver.rs); and the Host epoch SEQUENCE from the supervision record table (scm_launch.rs). The same activation contour renders generation= from a ResourceGeneration on its nonce records and from an epoch sequence on its activating/activation/fail records. Unifying them is a cross-file contract change.
key_meanings.artifact: artifact is NOT one identity across the corpus and this is a REAL RESIDUAL, escalated and not resolved here. It carries at least THREE kinds of digest: the approved executable / host artifact hash (host_job_launch.rs, kernel_activation_driver.rs, kernel_front_door_client.rs, launch_descriptor_validation.rs); the approved launch or bootstrap CONFIG-DESCRIPTOR digest (host_launch_options.rs, scm_launch.rs, launch_descriptor_validation.rs); and the SCM REGISTRATION CONFIGURATION digest (scm_launch.rs, hashed over the canonical registration rather than over a descriptor). launch_artifact_lease.rs makes it worse: its site binds a digest whose meaning is decided by the CALLER, and its callers pass image digests, config digests and a descriptor digest through the same key. Unifying them is a cross-file contract change.
key_meanings.phase: phase is a frozen per-file literal vocabulary, not an identity: 105 distinct phase tokens across the eight files. Two records sharing a phase token are the same boundary, not the same operation; `operation` and `fence` are what separate concurrent contours.
key_meanings.reason: reason is a per-file typed-kind vocabulary, not one corpus identity: three in scm_launch.rs (absent, mismatched, unknown), two in store_kernel_launch_sequence.rs (dead, unknown) and five in kernel_front_door_client.rs (delivered-response-unusable, unknown-binding, before-start-refusal, no-receipt-carried, activation-receipt-carried). A `reason` names only what its own branch established.
key_meanings.installation: installation IS one identity across the corpus: the Host installation identity handle, bound from the owner-held installation/epoch/registration handle on every site that holds one. Where no installation identity is in hand the slot renders the explicit missing marker.

What this fixture does NOT claim is that the surviving terminal is host-start-failed - on the production path it is host-open-failed.

correlation_contract: Every phase detail is rendered by LaunchPhaseCorrelation::render(phase) as single-space separated key=value pairs in correlation_keys order, phase first. Each &str value is bounded by host_diagnostics::bound_field; an identity the call site does not hold renders as the shared 'missing' value, so the emitted text carries exactly the markers listed in correlation_missing_markers ('<slot>=missing'), and is never invented, guessed from a constant, or left empty. The vocabulary has no pid slot: a reusable process id can never be recorded as a process-start identity.

front_door_corretirement.why: The retired pair claimed a disconnect the arm cannot observe. activation_response_or_reconcile is reached only when the lib.rs caller already got Ok(DeliveryOutcome::Delivered) from send_frame; a genuine disconnect and DeliveryOutcome::UnknownOutcome are both mapped to None by that caller BEFORE the call, so this closure never sees them. What the Err arm really establishes is that a delivered response could not be turned into a typed control response (receive or decode failed), which leaves the reconcile unsettled. The token is retired in the production code and named only in a retirement comment there, so no code emits it, and the integration target's case 978/9 front-door detail pin list now names honest_phase instead, with a separate negative assertion that both retired literals reach no emitted code.

inline_case_owner_cases_note: Every #978 forwarding twin is pub(crate)/pub(super) inside a private module, so no integration target can call one and never could: each twin's OWN rendered records are the inline owner case in its own file, and this map names that case per twin - the same mapping `inline_case_owners` lists, keyed by the twin rather than by the integration case that must cite it. The originals listed beside the twins in `inline_case_owners` are there because their inline cases really execute those original signatures, which is what proves each twin is behaviour-preserving beside an unchanged original. The case-3 and case-6 EXECUTED halves prove only the forwarding property on a reachable, already-forwarding seam - see executed_forwarded_correlation - and never a twin's own rendered record. Checked against real source, not trusted from prose: every case name here exists as `fn <name>` in the named file, and every twin named here appears as a call inside that case.
correlated_entry_points_note: SEVEN entries, one per twin that start_approved calls with the caller's correlation, and nothing else. The list is exhaustive on purpose: it is what the all-sites argument scan in the integration target walks, so a twin missing from it is a twin whose call sites and whose own emission sites are reachable from NO assertion on that contour, and reverting that twin to a fresh LaunchPhaseCorrelation::NONE fails nothing. The two approved-descriptor validators were exactly that gap - start_approved calls both with &correlation (host_job_launch.rs:1666 and host_job_launch.rs:1710) and both are mapped to their inline owner case under inline_case_owner_cases, but before this correction neither appeared here. Checked against real source, not trusted from prose: the fixture asserts that every entry here is a key of inline_case_owner_cases spelled the same way, that the count below is exact, and that the set difference against the delivered twins is exactly correlated_entry_points_excluded. The delivery's EIGHT twins therefore are all pinned, seven through this list and the eighth through forwarded_correlation_branch_contour, because start_approved never calls it.

correlated_entry_points_excluded.why: It is a delivered twin and it does take the forwarded correlation, but start_approved NEVER calls it: its only production call site is HostJobBranches::launch (host_job_launch.rs:1016), plus the original's own one-line delegation at host_job_launch.rs:376. Listing it under correlated_entry_points would make the start_approved all-sites scan look for a call the contour does not make and panic, so it is pinned on the contour that really calls it. It also binds no correlation slot of its own - see forwarded_correlation_contour.note - so it forwards what its caller bound without adding any identity.

forwarded_correlation_contour.forwarded_call_site_count_note: Every call site of the seven twins above inside HostJobBranches::start_approved's own body, counted from source: approved_locator_with_correlation 7, open_launch_lease_with_correlation 6, verify_launch_digest_with_correlation 5, kernel_arguments_with_doctor_anchor_with_correlation 1, launch_store_then_kernel_with_correlation 1, validate_store_bootstrap_descriptor_with_correlation 1, validate_eliotd_launch_descriptor_with_correlation 1. That is 22 of the contour's 31 &correlation-consuming sites; the other 9 are the contour's OWN host_launch_observe emissions, which the held_slot_bindings and bound_slots claims already cover and which are not forwarded-twin call arguments. Every one of the 22 is pinned: the argument read is per occurrence, so an unforwarded site names its own occurrence index and body line.
forwarded_correlation_contour.note: The counterexample this contour closes: the real calls that emit the locator, lease, digest, doctor-anchor, store and kernel phase records used to pass nothing, so render turned installation, generation and fence into `missing` on same-operation records whose caller already held all three. Each correlated entry point now takes that correlation as its FIRST parameter and each original signature is unchanged and still delegates with NONE, so the un-forwarded API keeps its exact behaviour while the approved-start contour forwards the identities it holds. Every value comes from a handle the caller already holds (host.installation, launch.authority_generation.value(), host.epoch.current.lineage_id); nothing is re-derived, probed, or read from a locator, lease, argv, nonce or path (I15.4). `approved_launch_paths` is NOT listed: it holds only locators and approved handles, so it still binds nothing on its own and never had an already-held installation, generation or fence to forward. RESIDUAL, stated not papered over: the rendered records of these correlated entry points are private-module and Windows-only, so their runtime proof is the inline owner case in each owning file (see inline_case_owners). This integration target can prove only the forwarding chain itself and the rendering property on the reachable seams under executed_forwarded_correlation; it does not claim a captured record from the private contour.

forwarded_correlation_branch_contour.note: The SECOND forwarded-correlation caller edge, and the reason it was a hole: HostJobBranches::launch builds its OWN LaunchPhaseCorrelation from the identities it already holds and forwards that binding into approved_launch_paths_with_correlation - a twin start_approved never calls - at host_job_launch.rs:1016. forwarded_correlation_contour above names ONLY start_approved, and its all-sites scan is scoped to that one body, so this edge had no structural assertion anywhere and reverting it to a fresh NONE failed nothing in this suite. This entry pins it: the three binding expressions are read out of launch's own body (its correlation is the Host installation identity, the lineage of the Host installation epoch it runs under, and the approved artifact digest of the exact branch it launches - all already in hand as arguments), and the forwarded callee's call site is scanned with the SAME per-occurrence all-sites reader the start_approved check uses, bounded to launch's own braces. NOTE the deliberate asymmetry with forwarded_correlation_contour: launch's contour binds no generation, because the generation argument it receives is an opaque identity handle with no bounded numeric spelling, so that slot stays explicitly missing rather than being re-derived or guessed - and the branch Job Object name, the executable/config paths and the raw locator values are likewise never bound.

forwarded_refusal_arms_note: Seven twins, each with the refusal phase literals that really occur inside ITS OWN body, counted from source and not invented: approved_locator_with_correlation emits substitution preserved 2 and locator typed rejection 3; open_launch_lease_with_correlation emits lease typed rejection 1; verify_launch_digest_with_correlation emits digest typed rejection 1; kernel_arguments_with_doctor_anchor_with_correlation emits doctor anchor typed rejection 5; launch_store_then_kernel_with_correlation emits store-dead 1 and store-unknown 1; validate_store_bootstrap_descriptor_with_correlation emits substitution preserved 2 and store bootstrap typed rejection 4; validate_eliotd_launch_descriptor_with_correlation emits substitution preserved 1 and eliotd typed rejection 1. That is 22 emission sites. Every occurrence of every listed literal is pinned, never only the first, so a twin that reverted one of several sites to a fresh NONE still fails. Note that the eliotd typed rejection literal is a DIFFERENT phase from the store bootstrap typed rejection literal even though both are refusals of a descriptor validator, and that neither descriptor twin appears in forwarded_reason_arms because neither one binds a typed reason.
forwarded_chained_correlation_note: Not every twin renders the caller's binding verbatim. The two approved-descriptor validators each chain one already-held handle onto the forwarded correlation and render THAT local at every call site: validate_store_bootstrap_descriptor_with_correlation declares `let descriptor_correlation = correlation.with_artifact(approved_digest.as_str());` (launch_descriptor_validation.rs:453), and validate_eliotd_launch_descriptor_with_correlation declares the same local through this cell's ONE composition of those slots, `let descriptor_correlation = launch_descriptor_install_correlation(correlation, launch, approved_digest);` (launch_descriptor_validation.rs:569). Every record either twin emits renders `&descriptor_correlation`. So a reader that demanded the raw binding name would reject a twin that forwards perfectly, and a reader that accepted the local name without reading its declaration would happily accept a twin that re-rooted the chain at a fresh NONE. This map therefore declares, per such twin, the local it renders, the binding it must be rooted at, and the EXACT root expression - and for the mediated case also the helper and the helper parameter the chain must be built from, because the helper is the one place that could be reverted to `LaunchPhaseCorrelation::NONE` and silently drop every forwarded identity without changing this twin's own bytes. The other five twins render `&correlation` directly and are deliberately absent from this map.
forwarded_reason_arms_note: Exactly the two Store liveness refusal phases, and the TYPED reason value each one must bind on top of the forwarded identities. The values are not hand-copied from an old fixture: store_kernel_launch_sequence.rs classifies the caller's StoreLivenessEvidence, whose two typed kinds are declared with the thiserror message arms 'dead' on StoreLivenessEvidence::Dead and 'unknown: {0}' on StoreLivenessEvidence::Unknown, and the sequence binds exactly those two kind names - with_reason("dead") on the store-dead arm and with_reason("unknown") on the store-unknown arm - while the Unknown PAYLOAD text never enters a record. Asserting only the .with_reason( method would be satisfied by any argument at all, so the value is required too. No other delivered twin qualifies: the other five refusal-bearing twins of this delivery emit no typed reason anywhere, and launch_descriptor_validation.rs has no typed cause enum, so reason is never composed in either descriptor twin.

unreachable_positive_arms: classify_host_scm_inspection Matching arm: ServiceRegistrationRuntimeInspection::Matching carries a ServiceRuntimeObservation whose fields are pub(super) inside eliot-platform-windows, so no eliot-host seam can construct it; only that crate's own tests and a live SCM readback can observe it

activation_response_or_reconcile transport-failure kind: no arm of this closure can name a transport failure kind, and none claims one. lib.rs:3411-3423 calls send_frame first and maps Ok(DeliveryOutcome::UnknownOutcome) and any Err(_) to None, so a genuine transport loss never reaches activation_response_or_reconcile at all; and lib.rs:3416 and lib.rs:3419 both collapse the TransportError variant into HostError::RecoveryRequired(error.to_string()), so by the time the Err arm runs only the erased text is left. The closure therefore records reason=delivered-response-unusable - a delivered response that could not become a typed control response - and proves no read timeout, broken pipe, SessionFenced, OversizeFrame, ZeroLengthFrame or UnknownOutcome classification. Separating those kinds needs the caller's error taxonomy or a new seam, both outside this issue. This fixture claims nothing about real Windows pipe, Job or delivery behaviour, which needs the live edge and #984's Event Log seam.
